prior_year_events.impact_description: Losses from these events contributed to elevated 2017 loss ratios and adverse technical results for marine and property related classes.

named_events.event_name: Hurricanes Harvey, Irma, Maria and Mexican Earthquake (HIMM)
named_events.loss_description: Losses from hurricanes Harvey, Irma, Maria and the Mexican Earthquake contributed to the 2017 adverse loss ratios; excluding HIMM the 2017 loss ratios would have been materially lower.

data.standardized_narrative: Opening gross claims reserves at 1 January 2018 were GBP 104.513m. Analysis of the gross claims development triangle (note) shows no material prior-year movement for underwriting years 2016 and earlier (net prior-year development ~GBP 0.0m). The syndicate notes adverse experience in marine/hull & cargo and property related classes driven in part by large natural catastrophe events in 2017 (Hurricanes Harvey, Irma, Maria and the Mexican earthquake) and ongoing volatility from unexpired risk; run-off related costs and reduced anticipated reinsurance recoveries were also highlighted as pressures on overall results, but these mainly affected current and open years rather than producing a material gross prioryear reserve movement.
raw_causal_phrases: recognition of future run-off costs and additional reinsurance costs
lower than originally anticipated gross premium exposure leading to reductions in anticipated reinsurance recoveries and expected underwriting profit
continuing volatility from unexpired risk and potential adverse reserve development
excluding losses from hurricanes Harvey, Irma, Maria and Mexican Earthquake (HIMM)
Hull, Cargo and D&O/E&O classes contributed GBP 18.3m loss on the technical result

data.data_quality_notes: Gross prior-year development was not stated explicitly in narrative. Prior-year development was computed from the gross claims development table (page 29) which shows no net movement for underwriting years 2016 and earlier; confidence set to 0.8 for the computed result. Note: the 2016 closed year has a reinsurance-to-close (RITC) arrangement disclosed elsewhere which can distort development tables if combined; the triangle used is the gross outstanding claims table and RITC effects appear accounted for separately.
